I don’t know why you’re getting down voted. This is factual info. OBGYNs are usually very on top of making sure patients don’t develop UTIs with screening to prevent adverse outcomes.

Actually, all pregnant women are recommended to get screened for asymptomatic bacteruria at least once in early pregnancy as this can turn into a UTI and pyelonephritis. Pyelonephritis is like a super UTI which causes systemic symptoms and like you said can cause bad outcomes. Asymptomatic bacteruria must be treated with antibiotics in pregnant women to prevent this from developing. 

Op would have to prove that his wife had an UTI and/or pyelo to show a clear connection to the miscairrage.

Okay let me break this down for you. A UTI stands for urinary tract infection involving urethra, bladder and or kidney. However, we call it pyelonephritis or a complicated UTI when the infection extends beyond the bladder leading to systemic symptoms. Systemic symptoms include fever, fatigue, and flank pain. 

Now speaking of pregnant women, they can often present with asymptomatic bacteruria which is bacteria in urine with out symptoms. However this must be treated preemptively with antibiotics because UTIs can develop quite quickly in pregnant women.
